watchdog_orgs_searched: Democracy for the Arab World Now (DAWN)
adversarial_framing_finding: General/Macro Press sweep surfaced the day's top Saudi geopolitical/security story (Houthi escalation, East-West pipeline strike, Saudi retaliatory airstrikes in Yemen). Checked multiple outlets' framing: Al Jazeera (Qatari state-funded), 2026-09-14, foregrounds Saudi-backed forces' airstrikes across Yemeni governorates (Mocha/Dhubab, Taiz) casting Saudi Arabia as a party inflicting harm; HRW (2026-09-15) frames conflict attacks as likely war crimes and names the Saudi-led coalition. In-window adversarial-framing item included as its own Negative Articles bullet (Al Jazeera).
notes: Coverage window dominated by the Houthi/Iran escalation against Saudi Arabia (Red Sea island seizures, East-West/Petroline pipeline drone strike forcing shutdown, oil price spike toward ~$110, Saudi retaliatory airstrikes in Yemen). Most in-window reputational hits are variants of this cluster, spanning distinct angles: territorial/security escalation (Guardian), oil-export/economic vulnerability (The National, CNBC, AGBI, Semafor), diplomatic setback with Iran (Foreign Policy), Saudi-as-aggressor framing (Al Jazeera), rights/humanitarian (HRW), and legitimacy op-ed (Eurasia Review). Saudi-owned outlets (Arab News, Asharq/aawsat, SPA, Saudi Gazette, Al Arabiya, ajel.sa, alriyadh) and Israeli outlets (Times of Israel etc.) excluded per source-eligibility rules. The al-Jawf prison-strike story and several humanitarian pieces (Common Dreams, earlier Al Jazeera/MEE) were found OUT of window (2026-09-07 to 09-13) and excluded on date.
